name: Soviet democracy
summary: Soviet democracy is the Marxist-Leninist model in which power belongs to a pyramid of elected workers' councils (soviets) whose delegates are bound by their electors and recallable at any time. It replaces parliaments with working bodies that make and execute law, excludes exploiting classes from power, and sits on public ownership of the economy, with the Communist Party as the leading force.
scope: The Leninist model as set out in Lenin's State and Revolution (1917) and 1919 Comintern theses and as codified in the 1936 Soviet Constitution and defended by Soviet-era writers. It represents the doctrine as its adherents state it, not the council-communist or anarchist federalist variants, and not the critics' view that the party hollowed out the soviets.

sources.usedFor: Bourgeois versus proletarian democracy, suppression of exploiters, equality, imperialist war, world revolution, communist majority in the soviets.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The 1936 Constitution guarantees citizens support in sickness and old age as a right, which Soviet doctrine presented as a state-provided service.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Not discussed as such; an adherent supports state wage-setting in workers' favour, inferred from the constitutional rights to work and rest.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Soviet doctrine rests on socialist ownership of land, industry and banks (Art. 6), with planned rather than market allocation.

public-ownership.rationale: Article 6 of the 1936 Constitution places land, major industry, banks, transport and communications in the hands of the whole people.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Not addressed directly; the aim is abolishing exploiting classes, so progressive taxation is consistent but secondary, inferred.

unions-good.rationale: Soviet doctrine treats trade unions as mass workers' organisations, though under party leadership rather than as independent bargaining bodies.

property-fundamental.rationale: Socialist property is declared sacred and inviolable, while private ownership of the means of production is abolished; only personal property is protected (Art. 10).

regulate-corporations.rationale: There are no private corporations to regulate; the nearest doctrine is outright state ownership, so a mild agree is inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: The constitution lists rights to support in old age, sickness and education as state guarantees, so cutting welfare contradicts the system.

worker-ownership.rationale: Lenin's Commune model has workers run society directly, but Soviet practice used state and collective-farm ownership more than worker-owned firms.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred: the suppression of exploiters and counter-revolution is defended as a duty of Soviet power, so security surveillance is accepted.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not covered by sources; a Soviet-era adherent would favour state restriction, inferred from the collectivist social order.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Article 123 makes advocating national or racial hatred punishable.

strong-leader.rationale: The Commune model stresses collective working bodies and recallable delegates rather than a leader bypassing the assemblies, though Stalinist practice differed.

state-harmful.rationale: Lenin insists the state must be seized and used for the transition, withering away only gradually; he does not call it harmful in itself.

limit-guns.rationale: Lenin wants the armed people to replace the standing army, but the sources do not address private gun ownership; adherents would differ.

empower-police-military.rationale: Lenin favours replacing the standing army with an armed people and smashing the old machine, so more professional force is disfavoured.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; the 1936 Constitution's duty to work and sexual equality suggest Soviet doctrine opposed it, inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: Soviets are built from factory and district units and delegates bound by their electors, though power is exercised up through tiers to central bodies.

rehabilitation.rationale: The sources do not address penal philosophy; Soviet theory had both re-education and repression strands.

traditional-family.rationale: The Constitution stresses equality of women and men in all spheres, which sits against traditional family hierarchy; family itself is not discussed.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The sources are silent; Soviet-era adherents rejected it, inferred from official practice.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not stated in sources; inferred from the constitutional commitment to women's equal rights in all spheres.

more-religion-public.rationale: Article 124 separates church from state and school from church and recognises anti-religious propaganda.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Lenin claims the Soviet system gives immediate effect to equality regardless of race and nationality, supporting active correction of inequality.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The sources state sexual equality but not a theory of gender; adherents' views are not documented.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Soviet doctrine supports national cultures 'national in form, socialist in content', but sources here only guarantee equality of nations.

gradual-change.rationale: Lenin demands smashing the old state machine at once and replacing it, not respecting established institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Internationalist doctrine opposes national exclusion; the sources do not address immigration, so this is inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Lenin looked to an international Soviet republic of workers, not to bourgeois bodies like the League; adherents' view of the UN is unsourced.

free-trade.rationale: Lenin sees capitalist trade tied to imperialism; the topic is inferred, not addressed directly.

nation-first.rationale: Proletarian internationalism and a coming world Soviet republic are put above national interest in Lenin's theses.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Lenin reads bourgeois appeals to democracy as cover for imperialist ends, so adherents distrust such interventions; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Eventual world Soviet republic implies open borders in the end, but the sources do not state it and adherents were split.

limit-growth.rationale: Soviet doctrine pursued industrial expansion; limits to growth were not a concern in the sources, inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic: the early sources do not address climate; planned economy allows it but adherents' stances are unrecorded.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Soviet doctrine prized technical progress under socialist planning, inferred rather than stated in these sources.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; Soviet state actually built nuclear power, but this is inferred from official practice not the sources.

revolution-justified.rationale: Lenin's theses state that proletarian dictatorship forcibly suppresses exploiters and that bourgeois states were created by insurrection and civil war.

experts-over-public.rationale: The Commune model has officials revocable at all times and paid workmen's wages, ruling out expert privilege; Lenin still allowed specialists under control.

central-planning.rationale: The constitution presupposes socialist ownership of the economy organised through the state, with planning central to the Soviet economy.

socialized-markets.rationale: Socialist property takes state or collective forms, and markets are not a core mechanism in the Soviet model, though small plots exist.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land is nationalised or held by collectives (Arts. 6, 8), so a tax replacing other taxes is not part of the model.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Article 10 protects the right of personal inheritance, while large wealth is abolished through ownership; adherents' view on a tax is unrecorded.

basic-income.rationale: The constitution links support to the duty to work ('he who does not work, neither shall he eat', Art. 12), which conflicts with unconditional payments.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: A state monopoly of foreign trade protected socialist industry in Soviet practice; inferred from state ownership of industry and trade.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State ownership of industry, banks and natural resources (Art. 6) places investment under state direction.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Socialist property is state or collective; small personal plots are tolerated but the aim is not wide small-owner property.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Lenin ties the withering of the state to a communist stage, but under Soviet practice wages persisted in the lower stage; the long-term aim is classless society.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Banks are state property under Article 6; abolition to leave money to the market contradicts it.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Lenin rejects class collaboration, and soviets, not state-recognised employer bodies, set policy.

one-party-rule.rationale: Article 126 names the Communist Party the leading core of all organisations, though pure council theory allows several parties; the tension is documented.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The Commune and Soviet model abolish hereditary privilege and rest on elected, recallable delegates.

democracy-best.rationale: Lenin holds that no 'democracy in general' exists, only bourgeois or proletarian democracy; adherents value Soviet democracy but not voters' choices unconditionally.

direct-votes.rationale: Soviets are working bodies with delegates bound by electors, not direct referendums; adherents differ on direct votes.

workers-councils.rationale: Lenin's State and Revolution sets out councils of workers as the basis of the state in place of parliaments, as stated by the Commune model.

right-to-secede.rationale: Article 17 of the 1936 Constitution gives each Union Republic the right to leave freely, though practice was restrictive.

natural-rulers.rationale: The model has all officials elected, revocable and on workmen's pay, rejecting inborn ruling capacity.

political-violence-never.rationale: Lenin describes proletarian dictatorship as forcible suppression of the resistance of exploiters.

war-builds-character.rationale: Lenin condemns the imperialist war that killed tens of millions for profit; glorifying war is not part of the doctrine.

separate-church-state.rationale: Article 124 states that church is separated from state and school from church.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Soviet law is grounded on the soviets' authority, with religion separated from the state and anti-religious propaganda recognised (Art. 124).

private-courts-defense.rationale: Lenin demands the armed people and elective, revocable judiciary as state functions, not private provision.

military-superiority.rationale: Defence is a sacred duty (Art. 133) and the Soviet state kept strong forces; superiority as a goal is inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Article 123 declares equality regardless of nationality or race, and the USSR was a multinational union.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Lenin's theses read bourgeois democracy and its overthrow through class conflict and civil war, which the doctrine takes as history's driver.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Rights to work, rest and education are guaranteed to all, but pay was by work ('to each according to his work'), so full equal outcomes are a later goal.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed in sources; republics had autonomy, but authority over traditional lands is not documented.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Lenin condemned imperialism, but sources do not discuss reparations; adherents' view is unrecorded.

civilizational-union.rationale: Doctrine unites workers by class, not by religion or civilization.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Work is declared a matter of honour and duty (Art. 12), and socialism is collectivist rather than based on self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The Constitution couples rights with duties of labour discipline and defence (Arts. 130-133), but does not explicitly rank them.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the doctrine treats nature as the people's resource under Article 6.

limit-population.rationale: Soviet doctrine did not favour population limits; inferred from planned-economy optimism, not stated.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Soviet socialism aims to advance industry under socialist ownership, not to condemn it.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Soviet doctrine prized technical advance but within planned institutions, so disruption of institutions is not wanted.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic and unaddressed in these sources.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; the Commune model puts decisions in elected recallable delegates, inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from state security priorities against counter-revolution.

restore-past-order.rationale: Lenin demands smashing the old state machine and building a new one, rejecting restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Doctrine insists on class analysis, rejecting 'democracy in general' neutrality; this is an inference.

direct-action.rationale: Lenin sought soviets and communist majorities within them but also used elections and insurrection; adherents split.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not stated; the Commune model builds new institutions at once but accepts coercion in transition.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Soviet socialism rests on advanced industrial ownership (Art. 6), the opposite of a return to foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Lenin spoke of eventual withering of specialised officialdom, but the Soviet economy kept specialisation; adherents split.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Communism's long-term goal is need-based distribution, but the constitution applies the socialist rule of work-based reward for the present.

production-for-use.rationale: Socialist ownership of means of production is meant to organise production for the people's needs, not profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Lenin's theses present capitalist rule as enriching capitalist groups through exploitation of workers.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Lenin's 1919 theses defend proletarian dictatorship as forcible suppression of exploiters' resistance.

collective-farming.rationale: Article 8 vests collective farms with land in perpetuity, though small household plots remain.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The 1919 theses say the 1914-18 war exposed bourgeois democracy and was fought to enrich capitalist groups.

taxation-theft.rationale: Soviet theory sees the public service as financed for the people's state, with no claim that taxation is theft.

harm-principle.rationale: Rights like speech are granted only where they serve the working people's interests (Art. 125), not by a harm test.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The Constitution grants rights as social and collective guarantees alongside civil ones, and ties civil rights to working people's interests.

conscription.rationale: Article 132 makes universal military service a legal requirement.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The Soviet model prizes voting and participation through soviets, not exit as the check on government.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is run as a working body of workers' delegates paid workmen's wages, not as a business serving customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Rights to work, rest, education and support presuppose material means for freedom; the Constitution lists these as guarantees.

media-academia-power.rationale: Lenin says press freedom under capitalism means the freedom of the rich to bribe the press, but not that media outrank officials.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Article 123 declares equality of races, and punishes racial hatred.

organic-representation.rationale: Delegates come from workplaces and districts through soviets, and the model pairs this with party presence, not family and guild bodies.

total-state.rationale: Lenin envisages the state withering away, though Soviet practice was heavily statist; adherents differ on the transitional state.

national-rebirth.rationale: Class-based internationalism rejects national palingenetic myths.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Lenin condemns imperialist aims; expansion is not part of doctrine.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority rests on election and recall by electors, not on personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Collective farmers hold land in perpetuity and citizens are formally equal; serfdom contradicts the Soviet order.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Lenin treats bourgeois freedoms as class-bound, which parallels the claim; the epistemological point is inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: Marxist-Leninist thought treats morality as class-determined, inferred from the 'democracy in general' critique.

single-common-good.rationale: Lenin's analysis sees opposed class interests, with the proletariat's interest prevailing over exploiters, not one universal good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Soviet doctrine treated Jewish national status through the Birobidzhan autonomy; the sources do not discuss Israel, inferred.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from class internationalism over ethnic return claims.

revive-national-language.rationale: The constitution recognises national equality, but language revival is not addressed.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Lenin's Commune model has working people run institutions through elected, revocable delegates from workplaces, and workers directly perform state functions.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education is a state-provided right with schools separated from church (Arts. 121, 124); vouchers for private schools do not fit.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Planned state economy has no deficit-avoidance norm, inferred.

economic-freedom.rationale: Lenin argues bourgeois freedoms are hollow under capitalism and political freedom depends on socialist property.

rule-by-example.rationale: The model rests on law, election and recall rather than moral example of rulers.

national-self-determination.rationale: The right of Union Republics to secede (Art. 17) embodies national self-determination in the Soviet system.

force-without-un.rationale: UN-era question; sources do not address, adherents split between sovereignty and bloc interests.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Anti-religious propaganda is recognised (Art. 124), pointing to a rationalist outlook, though not stated as sole guide.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Rights in the Constitution apply to citizens; the sources do not address immigrant eligibility.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Article 12 states work is a duty and 'he who does not work, neither shall he eat'.

class-collaboration.rationale: Lenin's theses present opposed classes and suppression of exploiters, rejecting partnership.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Soviet policy preserved culture through the state and education, and the sources show no iconoclasm.

dominated-front.rationale: Not covered in the sources; adherents of the Third-World-front view are not a documented part of this strand.

workers-nation.rationale: Lenin's theses expect proletarian victory on a world scale and an international Soviet republic.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Article 122 grants men and women equal rights in all spheres of life.

ban-interest.rationale: Banks were state property, which removes private lending, but interest as such is not discussed.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Article 123 forbids any privilege based on race and punishes racial hatred.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Lenin's Commune discussion describes the old state as a special force over a class, and proletarian rule as suppression of the oppressors by the majority.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Anachronistic; the sources do not address energy mix, though the state owns natural resources.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Doctrine supports national equality, so forced assimilation is disfavoured, though immigration is not discussed.

elite-replacement.rationale: The Constitution bars racial and national hatred and the doctrine rejects conspiratorial replacement theories.

proportional-representation.rationale: Soviets elect delegates through tiers by territorial and workplace units; party-list proportionality is not addressed.

national-mission.rationale: Lenin sought world revolution by workers, though the Soviet republic served as the example; a national mission is not claimed.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Article 122 declares equality; doctrine treats women's subordination as rooted in the old order, though patriarchy is not named.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Lenin sought to prevent officialdom privilege through low pay and recall, implying concern, but adherents defended Soviet officials.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic coercion is absent from the Constitution, which guarantees equal rights.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed; adherents' views on past abuses diverge.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Article 6 gives the state ownership of major economy and rights to work and education, far beyond defence and justice.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Article 123 forbids racial privilege and punishes racial hatred.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Articles 122-123 grant equal rights regardless of sex, race or nationality, though 'exploiters' were excluded in 1918 practice.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Lenin hoped for revolution abroad, while Soviet doctrine after 1924 held socialism could be built in one country; adherents split but the stated 1936 order assumes it.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Citizens' equality regardless of religion (Art. 123) and church-state separation imply one civil law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Article 124 recognises freedom of worship and of anti-religious propaganda, so conversion limits are not part of the order.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Nothing in the Soviet order suggests religious bans on slaughter, and religion is separated from the state.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Soviet party doctrine held that the state stays strong while capitalist states surround it, but Lenin in State and Revolution expects it to wither, so the strands differ.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Soviet power claims legitimacy by rule of the working majority, with delegates bound by their electors; the consent is class-based.

population-transfer.rationale: Article 123 forbids national discrimination, though Soviet practice included deportations.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Lenin defends forcible suppression of exploiters and armed workers to disarm the bourgeoisie.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Socialist doctrine replaces competition with planned work as a matter of honour (Art. 12).

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Lenin justifies suppressing exploiters' resistance and excluding the bourgeoisie from soviets, which includes banning counter-revolutionary parties.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not addressed; adherents define freedom through class power and material means.

separated-powers.rationale: Lenin's Commune is 'a working, not a parliamentary, body, executive and legislative at the same time', rejecting separation.

vanguard-party.rationale: Lenin's theses make winning a communist majority within the soviets the principal task of the party, in the Leninist vanguard conception.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The system aimed at working people's interests, with rights to work, rest and support, though not 'poor first' as a formula.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Most urban housing belongs to the state under Article 6, which favours public tenure over sale.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Not addressed; Soviet adherents regarded strikes as unnecessary in a workers' state but allowed little independent action.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Marxist analysis ascribes poverty to social institutions and class rule, not population growth.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Lenin demands elected, revocable officials rather than lottery, though he hopes everyone will learn to administer.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Lenin's theses justify forcible suppression of exploiters' resistance, implying suspending protections against internal enemies.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: State control of the economy (Art. 6) allowed price fixing; inferred rather than stated.

party-controls-media.rationale: Press freedom is guaranteed only where it serves working people's interests (Art. 125), with the party as leading core (Art. 126).

party-commands-army.rationale: The party leads all state organisations (Art. 126), but the sources do not specify command; adherents differ between party and soviet command.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Lenin says public service had to be done at workmen's wages, citing the Commune as the clearest sign of proletarian democracy.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The 1921 ban on factions, in force until 1989 per the Wikipedia article, made adopted party decisions binding on members.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Doctrine seeks an international Soviet republic, but the EU is a capitalist union; stance is inferred and uncertain.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The model has the executive and legislative fused in soviets and the standing army replaced by the armed people, so not a head of state commanding forces.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church and state are separated, and ecclesiastical government is outside the Soviet order.

clerical-rule.rationale: Religion is separated from the state in Article 124, which excludes clerical authority.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Lenin read the 1914-18 war as imperialist, and his 1919 theses treat it as exposing bourgeois democracy (s4); revolutionary defeatism itself comes from his 1914-15 writings, not the cited theses.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Press freedom limited to working people's interests (Art. 125) suggests censorship, but 'moral character' framing is not documented.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Recall at any time governs tenure, and the sources set no term rule; adherents' view is unrecorded.

recall-officials.rationale: Lenin quotes Marx that officials are 'at all times revocable', and Article 142 lets electors recall deputies.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Soviet doctrine sought alliance among workers' states; ending alliances is inferred as contrary.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Most urban housing is state property (Art. 6) and rented to citizens, so the order is not one of family ownership.

people-in-arms.rationale: Lenin calls for 'the suppression of the standing army, and the substitution for it of the armed people' (s1), but the 1936 Constitution in scope kept a standing army with universal military service, so the scoped sources diverge.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Soviet doctrine sought industrialisation; moral superiority of rural life is not claimed.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not addressed; national questions are subordinated to class.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Education is a guaranteed right (Art. 121) and its spread is valued, though intelligentsia suspicion existed.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Equal rights regardless of nationality or race (Art. 123) imply equal standing of peoples.

death-penalty.rationale: Treason is punished 'with the full severity of the law' (Art. 133), and Soviet law retained execution.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Sexual equality is constitutional, but the sources do not address school curricula.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: School is separated from church (Art. 124), and anti-religious propaganda is recognised.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from state control over press and Soviet moral policy, not stated directly.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Equal rights regardless of nationality or race (Art. 123); descent rules are not discussed.

minority-language-support.rationale: The multinational union recognises equal nations (Art. 123), and Soviet nationalities policy supported national languages, inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Law is uniform for all citizens, with church separated from state; exemptions are not provided.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Conformity to socialist labour discipline is a constitutional duty (Art. 130); eccentricity is not discussed.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Inferred from Lenin's anti-imperialism; debts of the Tsarist state were repudiated by Soviet power.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The theses argue that formal democratic equality is hollow without changed property relations, which transfers to independence.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Lenin dissolved the Constituent Assembly after the Bolsheviks lost the vote, arguing that soviets represent the people better.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Freedoms are conditioned on working people's interests, but growth is not given as the reason; adherents differ.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and anti-imperialism; the sources do not discuss aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Soviet defence is a sacred duty; the anachronistic nuclear question is inferred from the state's practice.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The model has no separate head of state elected from above; officials are chosen through tiers of soviets.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Banks belong to the state (Art. 6), so independence from the government contradicts the system.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Socialist property is the sacred basis of the order, and personal property is protected only as earned income and goods (Art. 10).

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The 1936 Constitution presents the USSR as a socialist society founded on socialist property, and adherents of the doctrine reject the state-capitalist claim.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Anachronistic and unaddressed in the sources.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred from solidarity among workers' states against capitalist states.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Article 18 bars changing a republic's territory without its consent, but annexation cases are not discussed; adherents split.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Church is separated from the state (Art. 124) and Soviet doctrine placed religious institutions under state law.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The model fuses legislative and executive, with no neutral head above party politics.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Article 17 gives republics the right to secede freely, so force to prevent it conflicts with the stated order.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not addressed; union republics have rights but one system holds across the USSR.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Authority rests on elected, revocable delegates, and religion is separated from state, so sacred rulers have no place.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from the system's egalitarian aims, not stated.

character-from-environment.rationale: Marxist theory holds social conditions shape people; the constitution's rights programme assumes social change improves people.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Officials are 'responsible, and at all times revocable' per Marx, rejecting a ruler above law.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The Commune fuses power in one working body based on the many, not a mix of few and many.

leader-cult.rationale: Council theory has no place for a leader cult, though critics document one under Stalin; adherents differ, so the answer leans to disagree.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Trotskyist critics say party leaders may restore capitalism, while official Soviet doctrine after 1936 denied class struggle; the strands split.

land-redistribution.rationale: Collective farms hold land in perpetuity and Soviet power ended large estates, as the constitutional order presupposes.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Article 18 and equality of nations (Art. 123) oppose territorial claims based on nationality.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Article 124 recognises freedom of religious worship and anti-religious propaganda, with no punishment for leaving.

women-must-cover.rationale: Article 122 grants women equal rights in every sphere, and religion is not to shape state law.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Unity is by class and workers' state, not by ancestry.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The USSR gave nations republics rather than only cultural institutions, but doctrine's formal stance on cultural autonomy is not in these sources.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Internationalist doctrine favours equal rights in the countries where people live, inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Lenin's theses ground political forms in class rule and property, treating freedoms as hollow without the material means.

ban-cartels.rationale: Private cartels vanish under state ownership, but competition law is not the Soviet approach.

no-bailouts.rationale: No private firms under Article 6; adherents' stance is not documented.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Lenin wanted an elective, revocable judiciary, which suggests courts accountable to electors, but liberal democracy is not the context.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The Constitution grants equal rights (Art. 122) but no quota; adherents' view is unrecorded.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Doctrine anticipates a world Soviet republic and cooperation, not autarkic blocs, inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Work is declared a matter of honour (Art. 12), though material pay by work was retained.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Lenin's theses stress winning majorities in soviets and mass action, not a small armed group alone.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Equal rights regardless of social origin (Art. 135) and abolished estates; the Commune model removes hereditary privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Internationalist class history is preferred, inferred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Lenin condemns imperialism and colonial rule as a feature of bourgeois states.

patriotic-education.rationale: Defence of the fatherland is a sacred duty (Art. 133), implying civic loyalty teaching, though internationalism also stressed.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The Constitution forbids racial privilege, but Soviet nationality policy used affirmative measures; adherents split, lean disagree.

public-money-creation.rationale: Banks belong to the whole people (Art. 6), so money creation is public.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Lenin sees capitalism's crisis in imperialist war and expects world proletarian revolution.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Doctrine condemns empire; influence in former imperial regions is not defended.

delink-world-market.rationale: Not addressed; Soviet doctrine sought a socialist bloc rather than delinking.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Lenin's theory of imperialism includes this idea, but the cited theses do not set it out; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Equality regardless of race, sex and nationality is a constitutional right (Arts. 122-123).

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The 1936 Constitution lists rights but they are conditioned by working people's interests and amendable by the Supreme Soviet; adherents differ.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Lenin condemned imperialist settlements, inferred; the sources do not mention treaties.

elective-rulers.rationale: All officials are elected and revocable in the Commune model Lenin endorses.

minority-veto.rationale: Democratic centralism binds members to adopted decisions, leaving no minority veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Doctrine justifies revolution against exploiters' states, inferred for a lawless ruler.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Lenin says the Commune is a working body replacing parliamentarism, with soviets as the basis of power.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The system abolished privilege and a duty to the poor from the privileged is not its basis, inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Lenin wants the majority to perform state functions directly, so participation is the norm.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Lenin says freedom of the press under capitalism is freedom of the rich to bribe the press, which matches the claim about media serving the order.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Lenin's theses argue that bourgeois democracy hides class rule behind formal freedoms and consent, alongside force.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Lenin's analysis of imperialism has capitalist groups enriching themselves from war and colonies, matching surplus transfer.

native-born-offices.rationale: Rights do not depend on nationality or race (Art. 123).

party-own-road.rationale: Official Soviet doctrine long expected other parties to follow Moscow, while theory allows national roads; strands split.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Not addressed; adherents' stance on aid dependence is unrecorded.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Doctrine rejects nationalist territorial claims; inferred.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Equal rights regardless of nationality or race (Art. 123) weigh against group leadership.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Soviet doctrine invoked antifascism, but the sources here do not tie it to constitutions; inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Adherents defend Soviet democracy as a genuine form of rule and reject equating it with fascism, as the article records the defenders' side of the debate.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Marxist analysis ties the Civil War to the class conflict of slave and industrial systems, inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The sources say nothing on monuments, and adherents would split between preservation and removal.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The sources do not address men's disadvantage; the constitution only states sexual equality (Art. 122).

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The sources do not discuss domestic violence; only equal rights of women and men are stated (Art. 122).

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Doctrine is universalist in claiming soviets for all workers, but accepts different national forms; split.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The Commune replaces the standing army with the armed people, with no guardian role above the soviets.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from sexual equality and the right to work.

office-by-exam.rationale: Lenin wants elective, revocable officials and wage parity, not an examined official caste.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The state owns strategic industry (Art. 6), so foreign takeover is barred by structure.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from sexual equality (Art. 122), though family law is not discussed.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Lenin quotes Marx that officials must be responsible and at all times revocable, and the soviet delegates are bound by electors, per the Wikipedia article.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Support in old age is a state-guaranteed right (Art. 120), not private accounts.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land belongs to the whole people (Art. 6) and collective farms hold it only as users in perpetuity.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Lenin rejects parliamentarism but soviets approve state action; budgetary rules are not stated.

single-official-language.rationale: The multinational union recognises equality of nations, which tells against one sole language.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: All land belongs to the state or collective farms (Art. 6, 8), so foreign ownership is impossible.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Not addressed; the Constitution bars discrimination by intent.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Work as honour and duty (Art. 12) is set against private acquisition, inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Lenin backs world proletarian revolution; supporting foreign insurgents was Soviet practice, inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Doctrine of secession rights (Art. 17) conflicts but Soviet bloc practice supported intervention; strands diverge.

corporate-influence.rationale: Lenin's theses say bourgeois democracy is a machine of capitalist class rule, with the rich controlling the press and halls.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from state control of press and organisations under Articles 125-126.

residents-only-property.rationale: Land is not privately sold, but residency rules are not discussed.

job-guarantee.rationale: The 1936 Constitution guarantees the right to work, with guaranteed employment.

democratic-peace.rationale: Lenin holds that bourgeois democracies wage imperialist wars, rejecting the claim.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Citizens have duties of labour discipline and defence (Arts. 130-133).

non-intervention.rationale: Doctrine backs revolutionary solidarity and the right to suppress exploiters, though sovereignty is invoked; inferred.

industrial-unions.rationale: Soviet unions were organised by industry, though the sources here do not state it.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Article 123 punishes national and racial hatred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Not discussed; Soviet law kept marriage as a legal institution, inferred.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Press freedom is limited to working people's interests (Art. 125); no access right is stated.

local-production.rationale: Planning favoured national and union-wide integration, inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: Lenin's theses make the party's stable majority within soviets the principal task, the opposite of informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The sources do not rank national over international law; adherents would split between sovereignty and internationalism.

religious-nation.rationale: Religion is separated from the state (Art. 124) and nations are equal.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Lenin's stance against imperialism and for equal nations contradicts tribute systems.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The unified planned economy shares resources across republics, inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Article 10 protects personal property in income, savings, homes and household goods while means of production are socialist.

defeat-communism.rationale: Lenin predicts the world victory of proletarian revolution, so an adherent opposes defeating communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Services are provided by the state, with no private or independent providers in Article 6's order.

religion-illusion.rationale: Article 124 recognises anti-religious propaganda, in line with the view that religion is an illusion, though the consoling-illusion wording is Marxist inference.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Marxist theory credits capitalism with building the material base for socialism, but the cited theses stress only its imperialist decay, so this is inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Article 122 grounds women's equality in work, pay and state provision, indicating that economic change underlies it.

socialized-care.rationale: Soviet doctrine aimed at socialised housework through state provision, inferred from the state's support for mothers and children.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not addressed; internationalist outlook disfavours it.

treaties-binding.rationale: The sources say nothing on treaties with nations inside a state; the constitution only guarantees republics' consent to border change (Art. 18).

cooperative-communities.rationale: Collective farms exist but the order is a unified state, not small self-governing communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: Equal rights regardless of nationality (Art. 123) oppose settlement to dilute minorities.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Adherents reject a third course; Lenin sees the proletarian dictatorship leading to communism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Class internationalism disfavours ethnic or religious land claims; inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Article 123 punishes racial hatred, and Soviet doctrine opposed fascism.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, with Soviet law varying across periods.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Lenin defends suppressing exploiters' resistance and excluding the bourgeoisie from soviets, though not all opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Article 124 recognises anti-religious propaganda, so blasphemy is not punishable.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Lenin condemns imperialism as capitalist groups enriching themselves.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Soviet doctrine is secular, and the state separated from religion.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Religion is separated from the state, and religious law has no authority.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Lenin's Commune model has the majority perform state functions directly through workplace and district bodies with recallable delegates.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The Constitution treats equality of sex and race together, but the intersectional claim is not documented.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Soviet-era practice.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Soviet-era medical policy.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Lenin insists on class analysis and the opposition between bourgeois and proletarian democracy.

alienated-labor.rationale: Work is made a duty and matter of honour under socialism; the alienation thesis is Marxist and implied.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Equality regardless of religion and nationality (Art. 123/135) opposes the claim.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: All power belongs to the working people through soviets (Arts. 2-3), not to God.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Church and school separation (Art. 124) implies a secular state, though dress rules are not stated.

social-market-economy.rationale: The order is state and collective ownership, not a market economy with protection.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Lenin replaces the standing army with an armed people, yet universal military service (Art. 132) shows forces are retained.

rich-first.rationale: Soviet doctrine aims at equal rights and abolishing exploiter classes, not a stepwise order of enrichment.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Doctrine took the side of the socialist state against capitalist blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: All officials are elected and revocable, so hereditary succession contradicts the Commune model.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Banks are state property rather than user-owned mutuals.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialism and the repudiation of imperial debts.

property-franchise.rationale: Suffrage regardless of property, race or origin (Art. 135) rejects property qualifications.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Article 123 declares equality of nations and races and treats national hatred as a crime, so the multinational union is presented as cohesive.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: The sources do not discuss trade-agreement standards; Lenin distrusts bourgeois international arrangements, yet adherents would back labour protections.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Lenin's 1919 theses call press freedom under capitalism the freedom of the rich to bribe the press and assembly a hollow phrase.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred: Marxism-Leninism treats women's emancipation as following from workers' power and labour, and nature as something to be mastered, not as a single logic of domination.

reification.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninist doctrine inherits Marx's view that capitalism makes social relations appear as relations of things, though the cited sources do not use the concept.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The 1936 Constitution sets fixed laws and courts, but the doctrine also holds proletarian power to be bound by no bourgeois legality; adherents are split.

racial-franchise.rationale: The 1936 Constitution guarantees citizens equal rights and universal suffrage regardless of nationality or race, and exploiter exclusion was by class, not race.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic: the doctrine favours participation through delegate councils and says nothing on the internet.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred: deputies must report to electors and be recallable, which favours accountability, but the party-led system kept records closed; the doctrine does not settle it.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The 1936 Constitution guarantees equal rights regardless of nationality, race or creed and separates church from state, so legal limits on marriage across faiths conflict with it.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Soviet doctrine treats national and religious discrimination as punishable and private shops as abolished, so a consumer boycott of a minority's businesses runs against it.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred: the model rests on elected, mandated and recallable delegates rather than representatives chosen by lot.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred: Marxism-Leninism is indifferent to reforming doctrine, seeing religion as something to wither, so adherents are neither for nor against.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Lenin's 1919 theses argue that under capitalism the rich control the press and political life, so formal liberty is hollow without economic equality.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred: Soviet law criminalised male homosexuality from 1934 and the doctrine as codified in 1936 did not support open service; the sources do not address it.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Soviet state ran anti-religious propaganda and education as policy, and the 1936 Constitution protected anti-religious propaganda while limiting religious activity to worship.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Lenin's State and Revolution holds that the state is an organ of coercion needed to suppress exploiters during the transition, and the Comintern theses defend that coercion.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred: power belongs to the working class through the soviets and is not divided among communities, although the 1936 Constitution did set up a federation of nationalities.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The 1936 Constitution guarantees material support in sickness and old age as a state-provided right, so doctrine favours state provision over charity.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred: Lenin's model relies on recall and binding mandates rather than term limits, and holds that delegates should be able to serve as working bodies.

vote-delegation.rationale: Lenin's account of the Commune has delegates bound by their electors and recallable at any time, which is close to revocable delegation, though not by policy area.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed by Soviet doctrine as codified; extinction risk as a policy priority is anachronistic to the sources.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The doctrine, as an atheist state ideology, gives no place to religious offices and the sources do not discuss them.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The 1936 Constitution gives women equal rights with men in economic, state, cultural, social and political life, which Soviet doctrine extended to the family.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred: soviets are elected by citizens under the 1936 Constitution, which does not provide for non-citizen voters.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred: under public ownership of the economy the state sets prices and housing costs, so legal limits on rent fit the model.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from Soviet practice, which kept author's and inventor's rights rather than abolishing them.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from Soviet practice of organising youth in Pioneer and Komsomol bodies led by the party, though the sources do not address it.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic for the 1917-1936 sources; the doctrine does not address nuclear basing.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from the Comintern theses' anti-imperialism, which opposes foreign powers' armed presence.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Soviet doctrine named Nazi crimes but had no general stance on formal recognition of genocides.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The 1936 Constitution states the principle 'from each according to his ability, to each according to his work' and ends income from exploitation.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Lenin's State and Revolution and the Comintern theses require forcible suppression of the exploiters and do not treat killing as ruled out.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred: the model is organised by class, not by ancient national descent.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Marxist-Leninist materialist view of sex as a biological given.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred: Soviet doctrine treated women as part of the working class and tied their liberation to class politics, not to women as a separate political group.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Not addressed; Soviet commemoration of the dead was secular, so a sacred cult of martyrs is inferred to be rejected.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The doctrine rests on historical materialism and class struggle over interests, not a spiritual contest.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred: the model is a state-power doctrine in which each republic is a state, not a cultural centre for a diaspora.

culture-before-state.rationale: State and Revolution makes seizing and remaking state power the first task, with culture following.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; Soviet doctrine was atheist and indifferent to how God is described.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed; religion is treated as outside the state's authority, so no test of scripture is stated either way.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Article 123 of the 1936 Constitution gives equal rights regardless of nationality or race and bars privileges for any group.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from the 1936 Constitution, which organises union and autonomous republics around nationalities.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred: Soviet unions worked under Communist Party guidance as part of the system, which the sources describe as party-led.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Lenin's State and Revolution treats the proletarian state as the rule of the working class through its own organs, so ownership without workers' power would not be socialism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The 1936 Constitution makes socialist property in state and cooperative forms the base of the system, which implies public control of essentials.

second-chamber.rationale: The 1936 Constitution created a Supreme Soviet of two chambers, one of them for the nationalities, though the doctrine opposed parliaments and the point is not argued.

municipal-property.rationale: The 1936 Constitution names state and cooperative property as the forms of socialist ownership, not municipal ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Lenin in State and Revolution defends centralism against federalism, so higher soviets bind lower ones.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from the constitutional principle of pay according to work, not family need.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed; Soviet doctrine favoured state medicine but gave no view on approval speed.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no clear doctrinal position is evident.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred: a state-planned economy with state control of money and trade leaves no room for untraceable payments.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from state supervision of speech and association under the party-led system.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred: the Constitution pairs rights with duties to the socialist state, and doctrine puts the collective ahead of the individual.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The 1936 Constitution separates church from state and allows anti-religious propaganda, in line with Marxist materialism.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from democratic centralism, under which higher soviets' decisions bind lower ones, so regional powers are not entrenched.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed; the Soviet record is mixed and no doctrinal position is stated.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed; no doctrinal position is stated.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The 1936 Constitution guarantees equality of races and nations and the doctrine puts class before race.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from proletarian internationalism, which treats pride in race as a bourgeois nationalist attitude.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred: the Comintern theses distinguish just wars of the working class from imperialist ones, so force is not limited to self-defence.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Soviet nationality doctrine treated a shared language, territory and culture as marking a nation, though class unity was held to override ethnic borders; inferred from the union-republic structure in the 1936 Constitution.

communal-electorates.rationale: The 1936 Constitution gave equal, universal, direct suffrage regardless of nationality, religion or race, so separate religious electorates contradict the soviet model of one class-based council hierarchy.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Soviet doctrine pictured the socialist state as surrounded by hostile capitalist powers seeking to undermine it; inferred from the Comintern theses' framing of imperialist hostility.

free-public-college.rationale: The 1936 Constitution guarantees citizens the right to education, including higher education, free of charge, as a state-provided social right.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Soviet doctrine relies on planned public ownership and direct state regulation rather than market price tools such as taxes; inferred from the constitution's socialist-economy provisions.

future-generations.rationale: Not a stated theme of the classics; a planned socialist economy run for the whole people's long-term benefit implies stewardship, inferred at low confidence.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Soviet doctrine stressed legal equality of women and men and class rather than gendered values; the 1936 Constitution's equal-rights article frames women as equals, not as bearers of distinct values.

arms-reduction.rationale: Soviet doctrine championed peaceful coexistence and disarmament proposals while holding that war arises from imperialism; inferred from the Comintern theses on imperialism.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Bolshevik doctrine denounced secret imperialist treaties and promised open diplomacy; this is inferred from the anti-imperialist line of the Comintern theses, not from a source I opened on the point.

capital-controls.rationale: Socialist ownership of the means of production, banks and foreign trade under the plan is the economic base of the Soviet order, which implies state control over capital movement.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The soviet state is a workers' state that disarms the exploiting classes and keeps arms for the working class's own army and militia, as in the Comintern theses.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Lenin urged soldiers to turn imperialist war into civil war, but a soviet state fights its own defensive wars; inferred and split by context.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Trade unions are mass organisations under soviet power that defend workers, though wages were set by the plan; inferred.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred: soviet doctrine replaces wage labour and market incomes with public ownership and state provision, not subsidies to low pay.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The soviet state plans the economy and credit in the public interest; legal limits on borrowing would run against that, and recallable councils decide such matters.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Comintern theses condemn imperialist exploitation of colonies, but the soviet model is about domestic power; inferred.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Lenin's State and Revolution chapter 3 argues the bourgeois state machine must be smashed and replaced by the soviets, drawing on the Commune.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Soviet democracy rests on public ownership of the means of production with central planning, a fixed blueprint rather than open experiments.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Marxist view that nature belongs to public ownership and from the rejection of market valuation.

sacred-nation.rationale: The doctrine is internationalist and class-based; nationalism is treated as bourgeois, with the Comintern theses calling for workers' international solidarity.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred: education is a public service in soviet doctrine, so student debt would not exist; cancelling it is consistent.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The Soviet doctrine treats national oppression as a feature of capitalism and denied it within the USSR; contested between doctrine and critics.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Marxists hold that human nature is shaped by social relations and can be remade under socialism; inferred.

public-service-media.rationale: Under soviet doctrine the press is owned by workers' organisations and the party leads it, so media independent of government is not the model.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Marxism-Leninism is atheist and the 1936 Constitution separates church from state; a belief that all religions share one truth is not part of the doctrine.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from the Soviet model of collective farms and state procurement that the 1936 Constitution protects; the doctrine does not use market-price guarantees.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from Soviet state practice of defending the socialist state against rival powers; the council doctrine itself is silent.

workers-own-party.rationale: Leninist doctrine holds the Communist Party as the workers' vanguard, but not independent of the party-state, so adherents would only partly agree.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the Soviet commitment to women's equality; FGM is not addressed in the sources.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The 1936 Constitution guarantees women equal rights with men in all spheres of economic, political and cultural life.

one-language-many-names.rationale: A linguistic classification question the doctrine does not address.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from public ownership of the economy and state planning, which replace private tort remedies.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from the soviet model of elected councils as sole organs of state power, leaving no place for hereditary or customary authority.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's subordination of individual claims to the collective and the planned economy; environmental questions are not addressed.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Soviet doctrine uses elected people's courts and fixed code penalties, but the sources do not settle this question.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Soviet internationalism promoted national languages while Russian became the common language; the sources do not settle a requirement.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Soviet doctrine treated trade unions as schools of socialism tied to the state and party; an open-shop rule is inferred to be opposed, though not stated.

voter-id.rationale: The 1936 Constitution gave universal suffrage to adult citizens without tests; a proof-of-identity requirement is not discussed and is inferred to be foreign to it.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The 1936 Constitution separates church from state and school from church, so no confession has legal precedence.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Lenin's Comintern theses reject bourgeois democracy as formal and class-based and hold that democracy is judged by which class rules, not by electoral competition.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from Soviet emphasis on women's equality; sexual morality was not addressed in the cited sources.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine that the state may suppress exploiters and counter-revolution; the internet is anachronistic.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: the state guarantees work, rest and support in sickness and old age as rights through public ownership, not through cash top-ups to a market economy.

women-suffrage.rationale: Article 137 of the 1936 Constitution gives women the right to elect and be elected on equal terms with men, and Article 122 declares equal rights in all spheres.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist-Leninist view of religion as a prop of the old order; the cited sources do not address women specifically.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from Article 123's equality of races and the Marxist view of ideology as class-made; scientific status of race is not discussed.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Article 122 guarantees women equal rights, and Soviet practice created women's departments; dedicated agencies are inferred rather than stated in the sources.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The 1936 Constitution makes land and the means of production socialist property of the state, so private claim-and-work title to unowned resources is rejected.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred: Lenin treats bourgeois institutions as instruments of class rule and soviet doctrine stressed state sovereignty, so adherents distrust courts above the state.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The 1936 Constitution separates church from state and guarantees freedom of anti-religious propaganda; Marxist-Leninist doctrine is atheist.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Article 122 of the 1936 Constitution gives women equal rights with men in all spheres, which adherents would carry into any autonomous arrangement.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The 1936 Constitution makes defence of the socialist fatherland a sacred duty, and Soviet doctrine held the planned socialist state must be defended against capitalist restoration.

indirect-election.rationale: The soviet pyramid sends delegates upward from local soviets to higher congresses, though the 1936 Constitution moved to direct election of the Supreme Soviet.

national-church-status.rationale: With church separated from state and religion treated as a private matter, no church could hold a privileged legal status.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The 1936 Constitution organises the Union around national republics and autonomous republics and regions for national minorities.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred: Lenin's Comintern line backs national self-determination, which adherents would apply to disputed territories, though the documents here do not discuss plebiscites.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred and split: anti-colonial doctrine condemns imperial borders but Soviet practice favoured stable inherited frontiers; the sources do not address it.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred: Soviet doctrine looked to rising abundance for all working people, with no ideal of limited needs or self-sufficiency.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred: the Constitution guarantees equal rights to all nationalities and free movement, and Soviet practice encouraged settlement across the republics.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred: universal military duty was framed in the 1936 Constitution as a citizen's obligation with men conscripted in practice, though women had equal rights in principle.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred: Leninist doctrine is materialist and internationalist and does not describe a spiritual bond between nation and land.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred: the 1936 Constitution protects personal inviolability, with arrest only on a court or procurator's order, though the sources here do not discuss the issue in detail.

close-ties-china.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Soviet foreign policy varied by period.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Soviet doctrine stressed self-determination and internationalism rather than a duty to kin abroad, but the sources do not decide it.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The 1936 Constitution makes land, minerals and waters state property, belonging to all the people.

self-ownership.rationale: The 1936 Constitution makes labour a duty and honour of every citizen under the rule that those who do not work shall not eat.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Not addressed; the sources describe public ownership, not tax structure.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred: the 1936 Constitution grants social support as a right of all citizens, not a means-tested benefit.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The 1936 Constitution makes the Communist Party the leading core of all organisations, and Soviet doctrine works through party and mass organisations, not around them.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred: the model rests on public ownership with no private business, so privileges for connected firms are not part of it.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The 1936 Constitution separates church from state and school from church.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Not addressed; Soviet doctrine favoured modernisation but did not call for a return to ancestral values.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The 1936 Constitution gives women equal rights with men in all spheres, but the sources do not mention divorce.

national-resource-control.rationale: The 1936 Constitution makes the country's resources the property of the state.

distribution-by-process.rationale: The 1936 Constitution applies the principle 'from each according to his ability, to each according to his work' and treats exploitation as unjust whatever the exchange.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Not addressed; Soviet doctrine held that racial discrimination was abolished and explained disadvantage by class.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred: Lenin treats law as an instrument of class power, not a claim of natural justice.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred: the state's socialist ownership aims at raising productivity and shortening the working day, but the sources do not discuss automation.

multipolar-world.rationale: Not addressed; the Comintern theses call for world revolution rather than a balance of centres.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninist orthodoxy holds that labour creates value, but the sources used do not state it.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The 1936 Constitution makes defence of the fatherland a sacred duty alongside proletarian internationalism.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred: Soviet doctrine puts the material interests of workers first and treats identity politics as secondary.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred: the model rests on public ownership of the economy, and Soviet doctrine in 1917-1936 treated market relations as capitalist survivals.

missingStatements.text: Freedom of the press and of assembly mean little while the rich own the presses and the meeting halls.
missingStatements.rationale: Lenin's 1919 theses call press freedom under capitalism the freedom of the rich to bribe the press and assembly a hollow phrase.

missingStatements.text: People who live by employing others' labour should be excluded from voting or holding office.
missingStatements.rationale: The Bolsheviks excluded the bourgeoisie from the soviets, as the Wikipedia article records, in line with the suppression of exploiters.
missingStatements.declined: Period-specific Bolshevik franchise exclusion, abolished in 1936; narrow, and the suppression and dictatorship statements already separate this ideology.

missingStatements.text: Representatives should be chosen through successive tiers of councils, from the workplace and district up to a national congress, rather than by direct national election.
missingStatements.rationale: Soviet democracy is built as delegates elected upward through tiers from factories and districts to a Congress or Supreme Soviet.

notes: Council communists and Trotskyists accept the council model but say the party displaced the soviets; official Soviet doctrine denied it. Answers follow the official doctrine plus Lenin's theory, so statements on party rule and restrictions reflect the 1936 order.
